subject: Multi-species, single-season occupancy model: error in quantile.default

messages.subject: Multi-species, single-season occupancy model: error in quantile.default
parts:
Good morning everyone,

My colleague, Michelle Pretorius, recently introduced me to nimble, and like her I am eager to explore its applications (previously I have used STAN to run my multi-spp occu models). Following in her footsteps, we have been trying to run a multi-species, single season occupancy model from Ponisio et al. 2020, whilst adding in parameters to estimate species richness, similar to Zipkin et al. 2010. To do so we are utilising camera trapping data from 3 sites, namely A, B and C. The data does exhibit overdispersion, and I have posted the full code below.

However, while running the model we have been getting a fatal error:

|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
|-------------------------------------------------------|
Error in quantile.default(x, 0.025) : 
  missing values and NaN's not allowed if 'na.rm' is FALSE
​
We suspect that this error is a result of poor model initialization, yet unfortunately we are unsure as to how to troubleshoot this. We have amended the code to not skip over NA records within the input count data in the observation model, as Andrew previously suggested, however this does not appear to have had any impact. In addition, we have noticed that using the direct run() function as opposed to runMCMC() appears to negate this error- but are struggling to understand why. As I understand it, runMCMC allows one to specifiy more arguments and it extracts the samples for you, whilst run() does not. Again, I believe this points to bad model initialisation.   

In addition, we get multiple warnings. We unsderstand that these can be overlooked: 
warning: problem initializing stochastic node Z[10, 57]: logProb is -Inf.
warning: problem initializing stochastic node Z[12, 57]: logProb is -Inf.
... etc... 

warning: problem initializing stochastic node X[409, 6, 18]: logProb is -Inf.
warning: problem initializing stochastic node X[409, 10, 18]: logProb is -Inf.
... etc...
​
Any assistance/suggestions would be greatly appreciated. 
Regards,
Zoe Woodgate
###########################################################################################
# INTIAL DATA PREP
###########################################################################################

# Load data
survey.data <- read_delim("obs_dates.csv", delim = ",")
survey.dates <- read_delim("point_dates.csv", delim = ",")
survey.cov <- read_delim( "habitat.csv", delim = ";")

# remove duplicate rows in dates column
# based on point column
survey.dates  <- survey.dates [!duplicated(survey.dates $point), ]

# add in random species that covers the stations with zero detections 
# 12 stations had zero detections
point <- c(145, 154, 156, 161, 174, 190, 193, 194, 202, 203, 229, 273)
date <- rep(NA, 12)
time <- rep(NA, 12)
species <- rep("random", 12)
individuals <- rep(1,12)
repetition <- c(11, 10, 10, 11, 11, 11, 10, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11)

# Make new data frame for these missing stations/points
missing.data <- data.frame(point, date, time, species, individuals, repetition)

#Now add them to original data file
survey.data <- rbind(survey.data,missing.data)

sort(unique(survey.data$species))
# random species is "species 36"

###########################################################################################
# HISTORIES (following Ponisio et al. 2020)
###########################################################################################

# Use function to create multiple histories for each species per site
histories <- createEncounterHistory(survey.data)
histories <- addMissingData(histories, survey.dates)

histories$X <- histories$X[,,-36] #remove random species 

# Check random species is removed
dim.names <- dimnames(histories$X) 

X <- histories$X

# nzeroes is the number of all zero encounter histories to be added
# Augments the original dataset
n.zeroes = 10

X.aug <- zeroAugment(histories, n.zeroes)

###########################################################################################
# PREP DATA FOR MODEL
###########################################################################################

# Pull out the number of unique points, species and # reps per station
num.species <- length(unique(dim.names[[3]]))
num.points <- length(unique(survey.data$point))
num.reps <- apply(survey.dates[,-(1:1)],
                  1,
                  function(x) length(which(!is.na(x))))

# Create a vector to indicate which 'site' (called habitat for ease) type each point is in 
# For each site, each camera =1, then other site = 0
# Repeat for all three sites
N <- rep(0, 451)
A.id <- c(rep(1, 119), rep(0, (451-119)))
B.id <- c(rep(0, 119), rep(1, 176), rep(0, (451-(119+176))))
C.id <- c(rep(0, 295), rep(1, (451-295)))

## Standardize variables
mpr <- as.numeric(factor(survey.cov$mpr))

tri <-  siteLevelStandardized(survey.cov$tri)
tri.linear <- tri$linear

msavi <- siteLevelStandardized(survey.cov$msavi)
msavi.linear <- msavi$linear

trail <- siteLevelStandardized(survey.cov$trail)
trail <- trail$linear

date <- surveyLevelStandardized(survey.dates[,-(1:1)])
date.linear <- date$linear

# NA's -> 0's
date.linear[is.na(date.linear)] <- 0

# Z data for whether or not a species was ever observed
# zs with 1s as 1s and 0s as NAs
class(X.aug)
zs <- apply(X.aug, c(1, 3), max, na.rm=TRUE)
zs[zs == 0] <- NA
zs[!is.finite(zs)] <- NA

model.data <- list(Z = zs,
                   X = X.aug,
                   mpr=mpr,
                   A.id=A.id,
                   B.id=B.id,
                   C.id=C.id,
                   tri.linear=tri.linear,
                   msavi.linear=msavi.linear,
                   trail=trail,
                   date.linear = date.linear)

psi.mean.draw <- runif(1, 0.25, 1)

# initial values

omega.draw <- runif(1, num.species/(num.species + n.zeroes), 1)

# initial conditions. 1 should be NA, NA should be a 0 or 1
zinits <- zs
zinits[zinits == 1] <- 2
zinits[is.na(zinits)] <- sample(0:1, sum(is.na(zinits)),
                                replace=TRUE)
zinits[zinits == 2] <- NA

# Make list of intial value data for model to call upon

initsList <-list(Z=zinits,
                 omega = omega.draw,
                 w = c(rep(1, num.species),
                       rbinom(n.zeroes, size = 1, prob = omega.draw)),
                 u.A = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 v.A = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 u.B = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes) ,
                 v.B = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 u.C = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes) ,
                 v.C = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 a1 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 a2 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 a3 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 b1 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 b2 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes))

# Further information needed for the model
constants <- list(num.species = num.species,
                  num.points = num.points,
                  num.reps = num.reps,
                  n.zeroes = n.zeroes)

################################################################################
# BUGS CODE WITH NIMBLE 
################################################################################

# Construct the initial values
ms.ss.occ <- nimbleCode({
  ## Define prior distributions for community-level model parameters

  omega ~ dunif(0,1)

  A.occ.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.uA <- log(A.occ.mean) - log(1-A.occ.mean)
  sigma.uA ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uA <-  1/(sigma.uA*sigma.uA)

  B.occ.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.uB <- log(B.occ.mean) - log(1-B.occ.mean)
  sigma.uB ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uB <-  1/(sigma.uB*sigma.uB)

  C.occ.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.uC <- log(C.occ.mean) - log(1-C.occ.mean)
  sigma.uC ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uC <-  1/(sigma.uC*sigma.uC)

  A.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vA <- log(A.det.mean) - log(1-A.det.mean)
  sigma.vA ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vA <-  1/(sigma.vA*sigma.vA)

  B.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vB <- log(B.det.mean) - log(1-B.det.mean)
  sigma.vB ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vB <-  1/(sigma.vB*sigma.vB)

  C.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vC <- log(C.det.mean) - log(1-C.det.mean)
  sigma.vC ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vC <-  1/(sigma.vC*sigma.vC)

  ## random effects
  mu.a1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a1 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a1 <-  1/(sigma.a1*sigma.a1)

  mu.a2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a2 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a2 <-  1/(sigma.a2*sigma.a2)

  mu.a3 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a3 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a3 <-  1/(sigma.a3*sigma.a3)

  mu.b1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.b1 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.b1 <-  1/(sigma.b1*sigma.b1)

  mu.b2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.b2 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.b2 <-  1/(sigma.b2*sigma.b2)

  for (i in 1:(num.species + n.zeroes)) {
    ## Create priors for species i from the community level prior distributions

    w[i] ~ dbern(omega)

    u.A[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uA, tau.uA)
    u.B[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uB, tau.uB)
    u.C[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uC, tau.uC)

    a1[i] ~ dnorm(mu.a1, tau.a1)
    a2[i] ~ dnorm(mu.a2, tau.a2)
    a3[i] ~ dnorm(mu.a3, tau.a3)

    v.A[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vA, tau.vA)
    v.B[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vB, tau.vB)
    v.C[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vC, tau.vC)

    b1[i] ~ dnorm(mu.b1, tau.b1)
    b2[i] ~ dnorm(mu.b2, tau.b2)

    ## Create a loop to estimate the Z matrix (true occurrence for species i at point j).

    ## A=2; B=1; C=0

    for (j in 1:num.points) {
      logit(psi[j,i]) <- u.A[i]*A.id[j] +
        u.B[i]*B.id[j] +
        u.C[i]*C.id[j] +
        a1[i]*mpr[j] +
        a2[i]*tri.linear[j] +
        a3[i]*msavi.linear[j]

      mu.psi[j,i] <- psi[j,i]*w[i]
      Z[j,i] ~ dbern(mu.psi[j,i])

      ## Create a loop to estimate detection for species i at point k during sampling period k.

      for (k in 1:max(num.reps[j])) {
        logit(p[j,k,i]) <-  v.A[i]*A.id[j] +
          v.B[i]*B.id[j] +
          v.C[i]*C.id[j] +
          b1[i]*trail[j]+
          b2[i]*date.linear[j,k]

        mu.p[j,k,i] <- p[j,k,i]*Z[j,i]
        X[j,k,i] ~ dbern(mu.p[j,k,i])
      }
    }
  }

  ## Sum all species observed (n) and unobserved species (n0) to find the total estimated richness

  n0 <- sum(w[(num.species+1):(num.species+n.zeroes)])
  N <- num.species + n0

  ## Create a loop to determine point level richness estimates for the whole community and for subsets or assemblages of interest.

  for(j in 1:num.points){
    Nsite[j]<- inprod(Z[j,1:(num.species+n.zeroes)],w[1:(num.species+n.zeroes)])
  }
})

###########################################################################################
# NIMBLE MODEL
###########################################################################################

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code=ms.ss.occ, 
                      data=model.data, 
                      inits = initsList, 
                      constants=constants)

nimbleOptions(MCMCuseSamplerAssignmentRules = TRUE)

customSpec <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, condition = quote({

  ## *********************************************************************
  ##  block sampler for species random effects for each species, RW
  ## *********************************************************************

  customSpec <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)
  sigma.nodes <-  Rmodel$getNodeNames(stochOnly=TRUE)[grepl("sigma",
                                                            Rmodel$getNodeNames(stochOnly=TRUE))]
  if(length(sigma.nodes) > 0){
    customSpec$removeSamplers(sigma.nodes, print=FALSE)
    for(node in sigma.nodes){
      customSpec$addSampler(target = node,
                            type = "slice")
    }
  }

  ## find node names of each species for random effects

  base.names <- c("a1", "a2", "a3", "b1", "b2",
                  "u.A", "u.B", "u.C","v.A", "v.B", "v.C")
  exp.names.list <- list()
  for(bn in base.names){
    exp.names.list[[bn]] <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames(bn)
  }
  if(all(sapply(exp.names.list, length) == 1)){

    ## base.names <- c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "b1", "b2",
    ##                 "cato.occ.mean", "fcw.occ.mean", "cato.det.mean", "fcw.det.mean")

    customSpec$removeSamplers(Rmodel$expandNodeNames(base.names), print=FALSE)
    customSpec$addSampler(target = Rmodel$expandNodeNames(base.names),
                          type = "RW_block")
  } else{
    for(i in 1:length(exp.names.list[[1]])){
      blocknames <- unlist(lapply(exp.names.list, function(x) x[i]))
      customSpec$removeSamplers(blocknames, print=FALSE)
      customSpec$addSampler(target = blocknames,
                            type = "RW_block")
    }
  }
}
), MCMCmonitorAllSampledNodes=TRUE)

# Specify which nodes the model needs to call
nodesToMonitor <- Rmodel$getNodeNames(stochOnly = TRUE, includeData = TRUE)
monitor1 = c("N", "Nsite")

monitor2 <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames("X")
monitor = c(nodesToMonitor, monitor1, monitor2)

customSpec$addMonitors(monitor) 

# Now compile the model
# Make sure the g++ file is able to be accessed. 
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(customSpec, enableWAIC=TRUE)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

###########################################################################################
# MODEL RUN
###########################################################################################

mcmc.out <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, inits= initsList, niter=10000, nburnin=6000, thin=10, nchains=4, summary = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE, samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE)
​

Hi Zoe,

Thanks for your message.

Let me give a quick answer by pointing you towards some similar issues that have come up on the list:

https://groups.google.com/u/3/g/nimble-users/c/ZZIn3gzKKuY

https://groups.google.com/u/3/g/nimble-users/c/9PmFGuJCrbg

Those illustrate how you can use the model object to inspect variables, log probabilities of stochastic nodes, and control calculations to isolate where something may not be fully initialized.

I am thinking it may be helpful for us to put some easy-to-find guidance up on how to inspect model objects to track down issues like this, maybe as a new example on the web site.  My impression is that perhaps users jumping over from other tools aren't easily seeing what can be done, but let me know how others see it.

Good luck and please let us know if those pointers aren't enough to get you going.

-Perry

    v.C[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vC, tau.vC)

    b2[i] ~ dnorm(mu.b2, tau.b2)

    ## Create a loop to estimate the Z matrix (true occurrence for species i at point j).

    ## A=2; B=1; C=0

    for (j in 1:num.points) {
      logit(psi[j,i]) <- u.A[i]*A.id[j] +
        u.B[i]*B.id[j] +
        u.C[i]*C.id[j] +
        a1[i]*mpr[j] +
        a2[i]*tri.linear[j] +
        a3[i]*msavi.linear[j]

      mu.psi[j,i] <- psi[j,i]*w[i]
      Z[j,i] ~ dbern(mu.psi[j,i])

      ## Create a loop to estimate detection for species i at point k during sampling period k.

      for (k in 1:max(num.reps[j])) {
        logit(p[j,k,i]) <-  v.A[i]*A.id[j] +
          v.B[i]*B.id[j] +
          v.C[i]*C.id[j] +
          b1[i]*trail[j]+
          b2[i]*date.linear[j,k]

        mu.p[j,k,i] <- p[j,k,i]*Z[j,i]
        X[j,k,i] ~ dbern(mu.p[j,k,i])
      }
    }
  }

  ## Sum all species observed (n) and unobserved species (n0) to find the total estimated richness

  n0 <- sum(w[(num.species+1):(num.species+n.zeroes)])
  N <- num.species + n0

  ## Create a loop to determine point level richness estimates for the whole community and for subsets or assemblages of interest.

  for(j in 1:num.points){
    Nsite[j]<- inprod(Z[j,1:(num.species+n.zeroes)],w[1:(num.species+n.zeroes)])
  }
})

  ## *********************************************************************

Hi Perry,


Thank you for your prompt response, and apologies for this delayed one. It’s been a chaotic time. We have spent this past few weeks attempting to both investigate the initial values by inspecting (and working with) the model object and determine the cause of the quartile error.

We followed both the nimble manual and provided examples, and have worked through some of inappropriate initialisation values that were present in our model. Additionally, we specified the original model further, and improved certain aspects (I can provide the updated code for anyone interested). With help from another colleague, we determined that it was not the original initial values causing the quartile error- runMCMC() works fine if we do not specify the model to monitor the “X” node.

Without this monitor the model runs to completion, and the monitored parameters converge. Unfortunately, it fails to provide a WAIC value, indicating that further latent states need to be monitored. The same model run on another set of data does not produce this error. We are currently investigating this issue further and will update once again we have figured out why, despite setting MCMCmonitorAllSampledNodes=T, WAIC is being produced as NULL. 

This thread has been incredibly helpful in this regard:

https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/issues/799


Again, thank you so much for your time.

Regards,
Zoe Woodgate

survey.cov <- read_delim( "habitat.csv", delim = ";")

                 omega = omega.draw,
                 w = c(rep(1, num.species),
                       rbinom(n.zeroes, size = 1, prob = omega.draw)),
                 u.A = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 v.A = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 u.B = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes) ,
                 v.B = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 u.C = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes) ,
                 v.C = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),

                 a2 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 a3 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 b1 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 b2 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes))

  mu.uB <- log(B.occ.mean) - log(1-B.occ.mean)
  sigma.uB ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uB <-  1/(sigma.uB*sigma.uB)

  C.occ.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.uC <- log(C.occ.mean) - log(1-C.occ.mean)
  sigma.uC ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uC <-  1/(sigma.uC*sigma.uC)

  mu.vA <- log(A.det.mean) - log(1-A.det.mean)
  sigma.vA ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vA <-  1/(sigma.vA*sigma.vA)

  B.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vB <- log(B.det.mean) - log(1-B.det.mean)
  sigma.vB ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vB <-  1/(sigma.vB*sigma.vB)

  C.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vC <- log(C.det.mean) - log(1-C.det.mean)
  sigma.vC ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vC <-  1/(sigma.vC*sigma.vC)

  mu.a1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a1 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a1 <-  1/(sigma.a1*sigma.a1)

  mu.a2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a2 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a2 <-  1/(sigma.a2*sigma.a2)

  mu.b1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.b1 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.b1 <-  1/(sigma.b1*sigma.b1)

  mu.b2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.b2 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.b2 <-  1/(sigma.b2*sigma.b2)

    u.B[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uB, tau.uB)
    u.C[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uC, tau.uC)

        u.C[i]*C.id[j] +

          v.C[i]*C.id[j] +

  n0 <- sum(w[(num.species+1):(num.species+n.zeroes)])
  N <- num.species + n0

  ## Create a loop to determine point level richness estimates for the whole community and for subsets or assemblages of interest.

  for(j in 1:num.points){
    Nsite[j]<- inprod(Z[j,1:(num.species+n.zeroes)],w[1:(num.species+n.zeroes)])
  }
})

###########################################################################################
# NIMBLE MODEL
###########################################################################################

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code=ms.ss.occ, 
                      data=model.data, 
                      inits = initsList, 
                      constants=constants)

nimbleOptions(MCMCuseSamplerAssignmentRules = TRUE)

  ## *********************************************************************

  sigma.nodes <-  Rmodel$getNodeNames(stochOnly=TRUE)[grepl("sigma",
                                                            Rmodel$getNodeNames(stochOnly=TRUE))]
  if(length(sigma.nodes) > 0){
    customSpec$removeSamplers(sigma.nodes, print=FALSE)
    for(node in sigma.nodes){
      customSpec$addSampler(target = node,
                            type = "slice")
    }
  }

  ## find node names of each species for random effects

  base.names <- c("a1", "a2", "a3", "b1", "b2",
                  "u.A", "u.B", "u.C","v.A", "v.B", "v.C")
  exp.names.list <- list()
  for(bn in base.names){
    exp.names.list[[bn]] <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames(bn)
  }
  if(all(sapply(exp.names.list, length) == 1)){

    ## base.names <- c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "b1", "b2",
    ##                 "cato.occ.mean", "fcw.occ.mean", "cato.det.mean", "fcw.det.mean")

    customSpec$removeSamplers(Rmodel$expandNodeNames(base.names), print=FALSE)
    customSpec$addSampler(target = Rmodel$expandNodeNames(base.names),
                          type = "RW_block")
  } else{
    for(i in 1:length(exp.names.list[[1]])){
      blocknames <- unlist(lapply(exp.names.list, function(x) x[i]))
      customSpec$removeSamplers(blocknames, print=FALSE)
      customSpec$addSampler(target = blocknames,
                            type = "RW_block")
    }
  }
}
), MCMCmonitorAllSampledNodes=TRUE)

# Specify which nodes the model needs to call
nodesToMonitor <- Rmodel$getNodeNames(stochOnly = TRUE, includeData = TRUE)
monitor1 = c("N", "Nsite")

monitor2 <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames("X")
monitor = c(nodesToMonitor, monitor1, monitor2)

customSpec$addMonitors(monitor) 

# Now compile the model
# Make sure the g++ file is able to be accessed. 
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(customSpec, enableWAIC=TRUE)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

# MODEL RUN
###########################################################################################

mcmc.out <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, inits= initsList, niter=10000, nburnin=6000, thin=10, nchains=4, summary = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE, samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE)

Dear Zoe,

It's been some time and I went over what you've described in these messages.  Are you still stuck?

It's true that runMCMC calls mcmc$run.  It then does some post-processing of results.  The error you are seeing from runMCMC but not mcmc$run indicates the problem is in the post-processing, possibly arising from NAs in the posterior sample.  If the error from runMCMC goes away when you do not monitor X, then I would guess X is not mixing.  In this case, turning off the monitor for X would hide the problem, allowing runMCMC to finish, but it would not really solve the problem.  If you use mcmc$run directly (and then extract samples using as.matrix(mcmc$mvSamples) ), you could inspect the samples.  This might help one see what the problem is.

If you are still stuck, can you send a fully reproducible example, with any data files needed, on- or off-list, reduced in complexity if at all possible?

-Perry

    v.C[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vC, tau.vC)

    b2[i] ~ dnorm(mu.b2, tau.b2)

    ## Create a loop to estimate the Z matrix (true occurrence for species i at point j).

      logit(psi[j,i]) <- u.A[i]*A.id[j] +
        u.B[i]*B.id[j] +
        u.C[i]*C.id[j] +

          v.C[i]*C.id[j] +

Dear Zoe,

It's been some time and I went over what you've described in these messages.  Are you still stuck?

It's true that runMCMC calls mcmc$run.  It then does some post-processing of results.  The error you are seeing from runMCMC but not mcmc$run indicates the problem is in the post-processing, possibly arising from NAs in the posterior sample.  If the error from runMCMC goes away when you do not monitor X, then I would guess X is not mixing.  In this case, turning off the monitor for X would hide the problem, allowing runMCMC to finish, but it would not really solve the problem.  If you use mcmc$run directly (and then extract samples using as.matrix(mcmc$mvSamples) ), you could inspect the samples.  This might help one see what the problem is.

If you are still stuck, can you send a fully reproducible example, with any data files needed, on- or off-list, reduced in complexity if at all possible?

-Perry

Dear Zoe,

It's been some time and I went over what you've described in these messages.  Are you still stuck?

It's true that runMCMC calls mcmc$run.  It then does some post-processing of results.  The error you are seeing from runMCMC but not mcmc$run indicates the problem is in the post-processing, possibly arising from NAs in the posterior sample.  If the error from runMCMC goes away when you do not monitor X, then I would guess X is not mixing.  In this case, turning off the monitor for X would hide the problem, allowing runMCMC to finish, but it would not really solve the problem.  If you use mcmc$run directly (and then extract samples using as.matrix(mcmc$mvSamples) ), you could inspect the samples.  This might help one see what the problem is.

If you are still stuck, can you send a fully reproducible example, with any data files needed, on- or off-list, reduced in complexity if at all possible?

-Perry
